video_title: Melo & Lethal Shooter Debate the GREATEST DMV Hoopers Ever & Say Michael Beasley Had HOF Talent

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on his strategy to defer to Michael Beasley
quotes.excerpt: I'm just going to give him the ball every single time so the defense can just key in on him.
quotes.quote: When I first came to the team, I wasn't the jealous type. So I said to myself, I'm just going to give him the ball every single time so the defense can just key in on him, because back then we didn't play regular teams. We had to play against Rudy at Spalding, we had to play against the whole Memphis team. We had to play against Richard Dorsey. Richard Dorsey is one wild motherfucker. He was trying to elbow people in the head, he knocked Kevin Durant to the ground, tried to stomp him out on the ground. He's just his own, but he's always on time.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on his development playing alongside Kevin Durant and Michael Beasley
quotes.excerpt: I wasn't the type where it was like, man, I'm older than these guys. Let me do what I know.
quotes.quote: What I learned back then playing with Kevin Durant and Michael Beasley, I wasn't the type where it was like, man, I'm older than these guys. Let me do what I know. I'm going to get you do your thing. And because of that, the whole state, I was number two in the whole state. Kevin Durant was number one in his position, I think Jeff was like number two behind Kevin, I was number two, and Merlin, that's Baltimore as well. And I think number one was somebody from Baltimore. I forgot his name, I think he went to La Salle or something. Ricky was like number five or ten, he might have been five. And Ricky was pulling from half court back then before he went to UMass.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on Michael Beasley's high school and college dominance
quotes.excerpt: I don't think people understand what Michael Beasley was doing in high school and at Kansas State.
quotes.quote: I don't think people understand what Michael Beasley was doing in high school and at Kansas State. It's unreal. It's like what he was doing, it's like, is this shit real? And that's how Kevin Durant and Michael Beasley was in high school. Kevin Durant would get the ball, same thing he's doing now. I'm not about to dribble a hundred times. I'm going to catch the ball, I'm going to go into my jab series. You back up, I'm going to shoot. You step up, I'm going to blow past you. If I come down in transition, I put it in my left, you back up, I'm going to pull. If you try to take away the left, I'm putting it in the right. If you go over there, I'm going to pull with the right. So it's like everything that he's doing now, he's doing the same. Same with Michael Beasley.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on Michael Beasley's missed potential as a Hall of Famer
quotes.excerpt: If Michael Beasley would have made different decisions a little bit earlier, you're looking at a Hall of Famer.
quotes.quote: If Michael Beasley would have made different decisions a little bit earlier, you're looking at a Hall of Famer, dog. I'm telling you right now, the stuff that I was seeing, and how much power Michael Beasley has, it was impossible to stop him, dog. It was impossible to stop him. So to me, in my own two eyes, and I area the greatest scorers of all time, to me, I think it's Kevin Durant, Michael Beasley, and Melo. Because you couldn't stop them unless you just foul them or try to hurt them.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on the lineage of small forwards in the DMV
quotes.excerpt: If you was a small forward, your lineage started from kind of that 90s.
quotes.quote: If you was a small forward, your lineage started from kind of that 90s. It transitioned, and it went from, you had Lonny Baxter and those guys who were small forwards, then Derrick Johnson came, he was a small forward, then Ronnie White kind of was a hybrid between the three and the four. So, the Beasley and Kevin Durant had to learn from the guy that came before you. So the Beasley and Kevin Durant had to learn from me, I had to learn from Derrick Johnson, I had to learn from these guys. And that's why a lot of our games are a lot similar. And Beasley probably was the last one in that area that's like that lineage of of of wings.

quotes.speaker: Carmelo Anthony
quotes.summary_phrase: Carmelo Anthony on Michael Beasley as a power forward evolution
quotes.excerpt: When I watch Michael Beasley, to me, he was a power forward.
quotes.quote: When I watch Michael Beasley, to me, he was a power forward. So I always had him in that box of a power forward that just he evolved the power forward position. That Amare Stoudemire type of power in and athleticism that can handle, that can shoot. But he had all the other skill set. So to me, he was a power forward who was evolving that position which made it so tough for him. When they started to put him in that small forward box, now you're looking at you as that small forward. Even T-Mac came over to that box, or he left the box and went over to small shooting guard. But we had to look at Michael Beasley like that, especially when you're in the NBA at that point in time where there are traditional power forwards. And then Amare comes in and just switched the shit up in the power forward. And then now you got somebody like Michael Beasley and Blake Griffin and them motherfuckers coming in who's who's evolving that position. Chris Bosh evolves the position, LaMarcus Aldridge, you know, so now everybody's evolved. So my point is always looked at Michael Beasley as that evolution of a of a of a power forward.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay on Michael Beasley's role in developing younger players
quotes.excerpt: He's supposed to be on a staff developing the next up and coming person that's coming.
quotes.quote: He's supposed to be on a staff developing the next up and coming person that's coming. To show, hey, whatever you have, Michael Beasley, give him everything you have. We need that knowledge. People like Michael Beasley, respectfully, he shouldn't be doing the stuff that they're doing right now. And it's crazy you said just Michael Beasley, like we can name a guy like Delonte West. Delonte West when I used to see him at Eleanor Roosevelt in Merlin, bro, oh my fucking god. It was like it was so effortless. Him and Eddie Basden. Yeah, him and Eddie Basden. It was they was Eddie Basden defense when I was growing up. I had to score, so me and Eddie used to work out together. You don't know who he is, but like, I knew if I can score on Eddie, I can score on anybody.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay discusses the trauma of growing up in difficult environments
quotes.excerpt: It's a lot of trauma growing up where we come from.
quotes.quote: It's a lot of trauma growing up where we come from. Both of my parents were heroin addicts, all my family in the streets. I grew up in a difficult situation. But the difference between me is, I understand with social media, if my brain or I'm feeling some type of way, I can't record myself doing it or put myself out there. And I feel like what me and him come from, sometimes people express themselves on social media, but people don't understand them.

quotes.speaker: Rudy Gay
quotes.summary_phrase: Rudy Gay advocates for supporting peers instead of mocking social media posts
quotes.excerpt: If I see Tom or Ray-Ray talking, I ain't laughing. I call you. I'm here for you.
quotes.quote: If you see a Tom or a Ray-Ray speaking from DC or Baltimore, people will laugh, but I can watch that video and I can feel his cry. So I'm the type of dude, if I see Tom or Ray-Ray talking, I ain't laughing. I call you. Hey man, I'm here for you. Even Michael, he's my man. When I was in Miami, he did a post, hey man, pull up on me, bro. I'm about to do a collab with Ashton Hall. I just want to see you. I want to love on you as a friend, because I want you to know you got a brother. I feel like the thing that I find cowardly is where guys from our era, they'll see that and they're laughing. What is funny? Reach out.
